live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: Project Hercules is designed to spark excitement and curiosity about astronomy by communicating the professional practices of observational astronomers, including the use of instruments like visible telescopes, photometers, and spectrographs, as well as participation in a community of scientists. Players will learn about technologies of astronomical observation, the data they are able to collect, and the various types of celestial objects they allow us to study.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In The Evolution of Trust, player's learn about the basics of game theory and the dynamics of trust and cooperation through different interactive modules. Player's are given the choice to cheat or cooperate with variants of personas- or strategies- to test trust and explore how it's built, evolves and breaks down in human networks.

Players will:

  • Learn the basics of game theory through the Iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma

  • Develop critical thinking about how trust, forgiveness, and retaliation shape group behavior over time

  • Analyze how network structures and Cultural Evolution Theory affect trust

wisdom-or-madness-of-crowds.card_title: The Wisdom and/or Madness of Crowds

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In The Madness and/or Widsom of Crowds, players learn and explore social network theory through a variety of interactives and puzzles. Using real-world examples and scenarios as context, players test connections and influence, and solve network-based challenges to see how ideas and behaviors spread across groups of people.

Players will:

  • Learn and apply concepts from network science, including simple contagion, complex contagion, thresholds, and bonding and bridging

  • Develop critical thinking and systems thinking about how group structures shape individual and collective behavior

  • Practice modeling and experimentation in a game-based context

wisdom-or-madness-of-crowds.card_excerpt: Why do some crowds turn to madness, or wisdom? The study of Network Science can guide us! To understand crowds, we should look not at the individual people, but at their connections

pick-your-plate.card_title: Pick Your Plate! A Global Guide to Nutrition

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In Pick Your Plate! A Global Guide to Nutrition, players explore how to build healthy, balanced meals using nutritional guidelines from countries around the world. Set on a global adventure across diverse locations, players will plan morning, midday, and evening meals while staying within a daily budget and meeting their nutritional needs.

Players will:

  • Learn and apply global nutritional guidelines by exploring food guides from 8 countries around the world

  • Develop cultural awareness and decision-making skills while selecting meals that balance health, tradition, and budget

  • Practice budgeting, portion evaluation, and nutritional analysis in a game-based context

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In Robo Sellers, players learn about money management and entrepreneurship by managing their own robot business. Set in a galaxy of alien planets, players will explore, trade, and build robots to grow their business and master key concepts of economics.

Players will:

  • Learn and apply skills such as profit vs. expenses, saving, investing, and loan management

  • Develop critical thinking, planning and resource management skills

  • Practice entrepreneurship by buying low, selling high, and crafting custom robots for profit in a game-based context

robo-sellers.card_excerpt: Play as a space-faring entrepreneur, and learn how to run your own business while you explore new planets, excavate resources, and build robots for fun and profit!

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In Magneto Mini Golf, players explore plasma physics and charged particle motion through the play of a 9-hole magnetic mini-golf course. Proton golf balls are putted through an increasingly challenging set of magnetic field configurations.

Players will:

  • Learn and apply concepts of plasma, charged particles, and magnetic fields

  • Develop scientific intuition about particle motion

magneto-mini-golf.live_description: Play mini golf on planetary greens with sub-atomic golf balls! Guide proton golf balls through the magnetic and electric fields to sink the putt.
magneto-mini-golf.card_excerpt: Play mini golf on planetary greens with sub-atomic golf balls! Guide proton golf balls through the magnetic and electric fields to sink the putt.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In Magneto Bowling, players explore electromagnetism and the motion of charged particles through seven unique games of bowling. Using a proton bowling ball, players arrange current-carrying wires to generate magnetic fields that guide the ball down various shaped lanes to knock over the pins.

Players will:

  • Learn and apply principles of magnetic fields, current flow, and charged particle motion

  • Practice predicting outcomes, testing configurations, and reinforcing physics concepts in a game-based context

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In Aquation: The Freshwater Access Game, players explore the real-world challenges of global water equity and resource management. As certain parts of the planet struggle to maintain freshwater access, players make strategic choices to build pipelines, conduct research, set policy, and allocate resources so that no one region becomes completely arid.

Players will:

  • Learn and apply concepts of resource distribution, environmental science, and economics

  • Develop strategic thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills

  • Practice balancing limited resources, adapting to unexpected events, and reflecting on high-impact choices in a game-based context

aquation.live_description: Choice, strategy, balance, and . . . water equity? Parts of the planet are struggling to get enough water. Use each region's wealth to build pipes, desalinate water, and conduct research to bring water where it's needed most.
aquation.card_excerpt: Choice, strategy, balance, and . . . water equity? Parts of the planet are struggling to get enough water. Use each region's wealth to build pipes, desalinate water, and conduct research to bring water where it's needed most.

walden-the-natural-world.card_title: Walden, A Game: The Natural World

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In this module of Walden, A Game, players take on the role of Thoreau - a “citizen scientist” - as they investigate the biodiversity of Walden Pond, collecting information and specimens of the many species of plants and animals to be found there, while being mindful of protecting the environment.

Players will:

  • Reflect on Henry David Thoreau’s work as a naturalist and citizen scientist. 

  • Articulate the basic concepts of phenology, the study of cyclical or seasonal biological events, and why it is important to understanding climate change. 

  • Gather phenological data about flora and fauna in their local environment. 

  • Apply an understanding of phenology to their own experiments around climate change. 

  • Demonstrate a respectful relationship to the natural environment.

  • Activity time: five modular lessons ranging from 20 minutes to several 60 minute sessions over seasonal gaps

walden-the-natural-world.card_excerpt: Players will take on the role of “citizen scientists” as they explore Henry David Thoreau’s contributions to our scientific understanding of the environment at Walden Pond and the effects of climate changes on that environment over the past 150 years.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In this module of Walden, A Game, players explore the nature of informed civic action within Thoreau’s hometown of Concord, Massachusetts, on July 4th in the mid-19th century. As they explore, players will discover issues around abolition, slavery, and expansionism facing the people of time and responding to them as an engaged citizen.

Players will:

  • Analyze the meaning of freedom in our society.

  • Identify issues and civic action around slavery and abolitionism leading up to the Civil War.

  • Compare and contrast writings about abolitionism and civic responsibility by Thoreau and contemporary authors.

  • Evaluate ways in which people can take civic action around issues that matter to them.

  • Create their own activist campaigns for issues that matter to them.

  • Gameplay time: 15-30 minutes

  • Activity time: five modular lessons ranging from 20-60 minutes each

walden-what-i-lived-for.card_title: Walden, A Game: What I Lived For

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In this module of Walden, A Game, players are asked to take a mindful walk around the Walden Pond, as Henry Thoreau did, stopping to appreciate the virtual environment around them. As they explore, they will cultivate skills for being “awake” in the present moment, as Thoreau described.

Players will:

  • Practice breathing and walking/movement meditation exercises.

  • Identify their sensations, thoughts, and emotions.

  • Identify and appreciate why Thoreau spent time outdoors.

  • Identify and analyze connections between bodily motion and mindfulness in literature, including Thoreau’s writings.

  • Create a trail map that engenders a sense of place and appreciation of the natural world.

  • Compare and contrast their own mindfulness practices with Thoreau’s.

live_items.body:

  • Gameplay time: 15-30 minutes with six options for related lessons and activities

  • Lesson time: seven modular lessons ranging from 20 - 60 minutes each

walden-where-i-lived.card_title: Walden, A Game: Where I Lived

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In this module of Walden, A Game, players are asked to explore the woods near Thoreau’s cabin, seeking the traces of the other individuals and groups who lived in the area before and during Thoreau’s time there. As they explore, students will think critically about the marginalized voices and stories that are left out of histories of this well-known place.

Players will:

  • Discuss the traces of previous inhabitants of Walden Pond represented by the audiovisuals of the game and by Thoreau in his texts. 

  • Compare and contrast differing perspectives on the history of Walden Pond. 

  • Research stories and traces of peoples who have lived in their own local area. 

  • Analyze whose stories may have been told about a place and whose stories may have been left out.

  • Gameplay time: 15-30 minutes with four options for related lessons and activities

  • Lesson time: four modular lessons ranging from 20-60 minutes each

walden-where-i-lived.card_excerpt: Explore the woods as Henry David Thoreau, seeking traces of the individuals and groups who lived in the area before and during his time there and reflecting on the stories in our histories that are not always told.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
Henry David Thoreau went down to Walden Pond in 1845 to live simply in nature. In this module as part of Walden, A Game, players take on the role of Thoreau as they attend to his basic needs of life in the woods for one day of his time there. They will explore the nature of Thoreau’s thoughts on self-reliant living as well as his critique of the materialist culture he saw developing in early industrial society in America.

Players will:

  • Identify Henry David Thoreau, his book Walden, and his historical/cultural context.

  • Analyze two key themes from the first two chapters of the book book: self-reliance & critique of materialism in early industrial society in America. 

  • Compare and contrast Thoreau’s life at Walden Pond to their own lives.

  • Imagine their own experiment in self-reliance and freedom from materialism

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In Morphy, players take on the role of Morphy, an alien who has crash-landed on an unknown planet and needs to find his missing crew members. The game teaches players about animal adaptation through challenging platforming obstacles that must be overcome by scanning animals whose traits are specialized to their environments. The scanned traits can then be added to Morphy’s abilities, empowering the player to successfully navigate the platforming obstacles in the game.

Players will:

  • Learn about animal adaptations and how their external structures help them survive

  • Develop problem-solving and critical thinking skills while navigating obstacle

  • Practice observation and application of scientific concepts in a game-based context

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
The Plastic Pipeline is a game that helps students explore real-world policies to reduce plastic pollution and protect our oceans. Set in the fictional world of Plasti City, players will investigate policies, interview characters, and uncover clues to weigh the pros and cons of different solutions across the plastic product life cycle—from production to consumption to disposal.

Players will:

  • Learn and apply knowledge about public policy, environmental action, and human behavior

  • Develop critical thinking and perspective-taking skills

  • Practice decision-making and problem-solving in a game-based context while exploring real policy debates

plastic-pipeline.live_description: Follow the trail of the life cycle of single-use plastics, and uncover policies that can plug pollution leaking into our oceans.
plastic-pipeline.card_excerpt: Follow the trail of the life cycle of single-use plastics, and uncover policies that can plug pollution leaking into our oceans.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In The Electric Shocktopus, players explore the real-world physics of electromagnetism by solving 15 puzzle-based levels as an electrified ocotopus. The player will navigate through fields and forces -overcoming obstacles while learning how charged particles interact.

Players will:

  • Learn and apply concepts such as Coulomb’s Law, the Right Hand Rule, Biot-Savart Law, and the behavior of conductors

  • Develop critical thinking and physics intuition by predicting how electric and magnetic fields influence motion

  • Practice problem-solving and spatial reasoning in a game-based context that simulates real-world forces of electricity, magnetism, and gravity

live_items.title: Curriculum
live_items.body:
Link to curriculum

Additionally, here are some examples of things your students can investigate:

  • Based on the Voltmeter in the game, what is the strength of the charges in Coulombs?

  • Based on how the Shocktopus moves, how strong is gravity?

  • Based on how the Shocktopus moves, what is the strength of his charge?

  • How about the strength of the magnetic fields?

  • Have the students make a level that shows off a concept (dipoles, shielding, capacitors, biot-savart law, etc)

  • Have them play the levels each other made!

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
Angle Jungle helps players build understanding of basic geometry concepts through puzzle-based gameplay. Set in a vibrant jungle world, players solve challenges that require identifying, measuring, and reasoning with angles to activate gems and unlock a new level.

Players will:

  • Learn and apply concepts such as positive and negative angles, clockwise and anticlockwise rotation, and angles greater than 180 degrees

  • Develop skills in problem-solving mathematical situations

  • Practice using tools like the protractor in a game-based context

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
Infosphere Invaders puts players in the role of commanding a team of agents aboard a spaceship. Players will combat disinformation threats across three distinct scenarios, each featuring formidable bosses. By engaging with the game's challenges, which are inspired by real-life disinformation campaigns, students will gain valuable insights into the complexities of disinformation policy and develop critical thinking skills to navigate the rapidly changing digital landscape.

Players will:

  • Learn and apply key concepts in media literacy, policy, and civic engagement

  • Develop critical thinking skills to navigate the rapidly changing digital landscape

  • Practice evaluating information, recognizing patterns, and strategizing in a game-based context

infosphere-invaders.live_description: Play as an all star agent team that works together to de-escalate disinformation threats made by The Divider, The Misleader, and The Bot Master in the infosphere.
infosphere-invaders.card_excerpt: Play as an all star agent team that works together to de-escalate disinformation threats made by The Divider, The Misleader, and The Bot Master in the infosphere.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In Cozy River Valley, the player takes on the role of a young farmer who must navigate obstacles and opportunities with water management that shape the future their career and generational land. By playing through years of changing seasons, the player must balance water consumption, community, environment, and financial well-being with strategy and consideration.

Players will:

Learn how water is used in agriculture and the interconnectedness of surface water, groundwater, and precipitation/climate.

Develop systems thinking, critical reasoning, and an understanding of sustainability principles

Practice decision-making to meet personal, environmental, and community needs

cozy-river-valley.live_description: Manage your farm, build community and create balance with nature and water. Can your farm survive in challenging times?
cozy-river-valley.card_excerpt: Manage your farm, build community and create balance with nature and water. Can your farm survive in challenging times?

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In Velocity Raptor, players traverse through a challenging variety of physics puzzles based on the theory and properties of Special Relativity. Set in of lair of levels where the player approach’s the speed of light, players will explore the results of relativistic motion through time dilation, length contraction, the Doppler effect, and various paradoxes in order to progress.

Players will:

  • Learn and apply the Lorentz Equations to analyze changes in space, time, and frequency at relativistic speeds

  • Develop scientific reasoning, quantitative problem-solving, and conceptual modeling skills

  • Practice analyzing accurate physics simulations and predicting outcomes based on given properties

velocity-raptor.card_excerpt: Velocity Raptor must travel near the speed of light to save the world! Take on an adventure in 2+1 dimensions, in the the Lair of relativity

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In That’s Your Right, players engage in a competitive card game to understand the meaning and importance of the Bill of Rights. Players will analyze, compare, and apply constitutional principles through the play of tokens and cards to gain points over their opponent.

Players will:

  • Learn and apply knowledge of the essential liberties protected in the Bill of Rights

  • Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating the importance of each amendment and making connections to everyday life scenarios

  • Practice applying constitutional principles that safeguards freedoms and protects citizens from government intrusion

thats-your-right.live_description: A challenging, fun card game that helps students learn about their rights under the Bill of Rights, the first 10 amendments to the Constitution.
thats-your-right.card_excerpt: A challenging, fun card game that helps students learn about their rights under the Bill of Rights, the first 10 amendments to the Constitution.

live_items.body: Theme Park Kitchen supports food safety learning for middle school youth. This fun, multi-level game teaches safe food handling, including handwashing, cooking foods to the proper temperature and avoiding cross-contamination.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
It's 1774 in Williamsburg, and tensions in the British American Colonies are rising. Your students are invited to engage with young people around the city to see if independence is in the air... or not?

Uncovering Loyalties with Colonial Williamsburg puts them at the center of the action in pre-revolutionary Virginia. Commissioned by Lord Dunmore, students will ask questions, listen to responses, and apply critical-thinking skills to identify where loyalties lie.

Your students will discover how history is always more interesting… once they start asking questions.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: In Mission to the Mesozoic, step into the role of a time-traveling photographer and explore Earth’s prehistoric landscapes! Partner with a scientist to journey through the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods, where you'll identify and photograph diverse plants and animals. As you complete each quest, look for connections between different time periods and uncover relationships in the ancient ecosystems. This immersive game challenges players to link environmental features and build a deeper understanding of Earth's evolutionary past.

mission-to-the-mesozoic.live_description: Travel back in time as a photographer in *Mission to the Mesozoic*! Explore the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods, capturing photos and discovering connections between ancient flora and fauna.
mission-to-the-mesozoic.card_excerpt: Travel back in time as a photographer in *Mission to the Mesozoic*! Explore the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods, capturing photos and discovering connections between ancient flora and fauna.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: In EcoKingdoms, step into the role of a park manager and navigate the challenges of balancing wildlife, plant conservation, tourism, and budget. Each decision you make impacts these four key components, so choose wisely to ensure the park’s success. With each scenario, you'll face unique challenges, requiring you to weigh the effects on animal and plant life, visitor satisfaction, and park finances. Keep an eye on your component levels, adapt to changing situations, and lead your park to a sustainable future!

ecokingdoms.live_description: Manage a park and balance the needs of animal life, plant life, tourism, and finances. Make smart choices to keep your park thriving in EcoKingdoms!
ecokingdoms.card_excerpt: Manage a park and balance the needs of animal life, plant life, tourism, and finances. Make smart choices to keep your park thriving in EcoKingdoms!

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: Get ready to defend your ship and prove your typing skills in this thrilling typing game! Type the words next to each enemy ship or missile to shoot them down with plasma bullets before they hit you. As you progress through the levels, you'll face larger enemy ships with more difficult words, as well as projectiles that need to be destroyed. If things get too intense, deploy EMP bombs to clear the area of enemies. With each level getting harder, you'll need to improve your typing speed and accuracy to survive the waves of attacks. Can you defeat the enemy fleet and master the art of typing under pressure?

ztype.card_excerpt: Improve your typing speed and accuracy in this action-packed game! Type words to fire plasma bullets and destroy enemy ships while fending off waves of attacks. Can you survive the challenge?

live_items.body: Wave on a String invites you to explore the physics of waves in an interactive way! Create waves by wiggling the string, or experiment with the frequency and amplitude of an oscillator to see how waves change in response. Perfect for anyone curious about wave dynamics, this simulation lets you visualize and understand wave properties in a fun and engaging environment. Whether you're adjusting the speed or amplitude, you’ll discover how waves behave in different scenarios!

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: In Unit Rates, you’ll master the art of calculating and comparing unit rates in fun, everyday scenarios like shopping for fruits, vegetables, and candy or racing cars on the track. Build a double number line to identify patterns, interpret ratios with mixed units, and explore how changing the numerator or denominator affects the unit rate. Through hands-on problem solving, you'll develop strategies to compare rates and tackle real-world challenges. Whether you're at the store or on the race track, Unit Rates makes learning math engaging and practical!

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: The Fiscal Ship challenges you to put the federal budget on a sustainable course. Your mission is to pick from a menu of tax and spending options to reduce the debt from projected levels over the next 25 years. Small changes to spending and taxes won’t suffice. The choices are difficult, but the goal is achievable.

live_items.body:
Tami’s Tower is an educational engineering design game in which the player learns how to design a solution to a problem using basic engineering design principles.

Tami's Tower is part of the Yard Games, our collection of middle school science games. Designed as playful introductions to complex topics, the games are online and free to play.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: States of Matter lets you dive into the fascinating world of solids, liquids, and gases! Experiment with heating, cooling, and compressing atoms and molecules to see how they change between phases. Compare how particles behave in different states and discover how varying temperature and pressure affects their movement. Learn the molecular details behind freezing, melting, and boiling, and understand that different substances have unique properties like melting and boiling points. It’s an engaging way to explore the science of matter at a molecular level!

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: In Projectile Motion, fire everyday objects from a cannon and challenge yourself to hit a target! Experiment with variables like launch angle, initial speed, and height to observe how they affect the trajectory of a projectile. Learn how the x and y motions are independent, and explore the impact of air resistance on velocity and acceleration. Whether you’re estimating where an object will land or investigating the effects of drag force, this interactive simulation offers a fun and educational way to master the principles of projectile motion.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: In Pendulum Lab, explore the physics of pendulums by designing your own experiments. Adjust variables like length, mass, and angle to see how they affect the pendulum's period, and learn about the small-angle approximation. Dive into concepts like the conservation of mechanical energy, using kinetic and potential energy to understand the pendulum’s motion. You can even take your experiment to the moon or Planet X and determine the value of gravitational acceleration there! Whether you're studying energy graphs or testing physics principles, Pendulum Lab offers a hands-on way to explore the science of motion.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: In Molecules and Light, uncover the science behind how light interacts with atmospheric molecules. Learn how the absorption of light varies depending on the type of molecule and the kind of light, and observe how energy increases from microwave to ultraviolet. Predict how different wavelengths of light affect the motion of molecules and understand how molecular structure influences these interactions. Whether you're curious about greenhouse gases or the ozone layer, this simulation provides an engaging way to explore the role of light in our atmosphere and its impact on climate.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: Put your understanding of the states of matter to the test with Matter Sorter! In this fast-paced, Tetris-like game, objects fall from the top of the screen, and it’s your job to sort them into the correct bins: solid, liquid, gas, or plasma. Each level gets faster, and you can only make a few mistakes before it’s game over. Learn what makes plasmas unique and discover where you can find them in nature, like in the Sun and the Northern Lights. Think fast, sort accurately, and see how far you can go in this thrilling scientific challenge!

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: In Graphing Lines, dive into the fundamentals of linear equations and their graphs. Learn how to compute the slope of a line, graph lines from equations in slope-intercept or point-slope form, and write equations from a graphed line. Experiment with changing variables in a linear equation and predict how they affect the line’s graph. Whether you're practicing graphing skills or taking on challenges in the line game, this interactive tool is perfect for mastering the concepts of slope and linear equations.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: Flap to the Future, created by Cornell Lab's Bird Academy, lets players experience the evolutionary milestones that led to modern bird flight. Starting as a dinosaur, you’ll glide as Microraptor, fly as an American Robin, and explore the possibilities of future bird evolution. Each level highlights how key adaptations like feathers and flight muscles developed, reflecting real scientific debates and discoveries. Players will investigate the benefits and challenges of these adaptations as they control their bird’s journey through time and ecosystems.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: In Energy Skate Park: Basics, discover the principles of mechanical energy conservation as you guide a skater through different tracks. Learn how kinetic energy (KE) and gravitational potential energy (PE) change as the skater moves, and explore how mass and friction affect energy levels. Use energy bar and pie charts to predict the skater's speed or position, and calculate energy values at different points on the track. Design your own skate park, complete with ramps and jumps, and see energy conservation in action!

live_items.body: In Concentration, explore the relationship between solute, volume, and solution concentration. Watch as the solution changes color with increasing concentration and predict how adding or removing water, solute, or solution affects the concentration. Design your own procedures to create solutions of specific concentrations or adjust existing ones. Test how far you can go before reaching saturation, and experiment with different actions to see how they impact the concentration levels of your solutions!

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: In Color Vision, experiment with mixing red, green, and blue light to see how different combinations create a full spectrum of colors. Learn how light behaves as it passes through colored filters and how it affects the colors we perceive. Whether you’re viewing light as beams or photons, this interactive experience helps you understand the science of color and how our eyes interpret various light sources. Create your own rainbow and uncover the magic of color vision!

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: In Circuit Construction Kit: DC, experiment with basic electricity by designing and building circuits from scratch. Use tools like ammeters and voltmeters to measure current and voltage, and learn how electricity flows in both series and parallel circuits. Test common objects to determine if they are conductors or insulators, and explore the relationships between voltage, current, and resistance. Whether you’re following schematic drawings or creating your own designs, this interactive kit provides a hands-on way to understand the fundamentals of electricity!

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: In Bending Light, discover the science behind how light changes direction as it moves from one material to another. Experiment with prisms to create rainbows, and explore how the speed and wavelength of light affect the angle of refraction. Use Snell’s law to predict how light will bend, and learn how different wavelengths of light are refracted at different angles. Whether you’re playing with lasers or building rainbows, this interactive tool makes learning about light and refraction fun and engaging!

live_items.body: BeastBox, a collaboration between the Cornell Lab of Ornithology and wildlife DJ Ben Mirin, lets you mix wild animal voices with beatbox rhythms to create unique music. Travel through ecosystems, unlocking new sounds and musical layers as you add animals from the same habitat. With every mix, you’ll explore the connection between nature and rhythm while unlocking Beast Mode for an extra musical challenge.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: Battleship Numberline is an exciting and educational game designed to build number sense by challenging players to estimate positions on a number line. As you destroy paper ships and collect stars, you'll practice comparing whole numbers, fractions, and decimals. Ideal for developing key numerical skills, the game also offers interactive feedback with worked examples when mistakes are made, helping you learn from your errors. Whether you're a student or just looking to improve your math skills, Battleship Numberline makes learning number sense fun, effective, and engaging!

live_items.body: In Balancing Act, explore the principles of balance by placing objects of various masses on a plank. Predict how changing the position or weight of objects will make the plank tilt or stay balanced. Develop rules to understand the relationship between mass, distance, and balance, and apply your knowledge to solve puzzles. Test what you’ve learned in the Balance Challenge game and see how well you can maintain equilibrium in this fun, interactive experience!

Count unit squares to find the area of simple shapes or decompose irregular shapes into smaller, regular ones like rectangles and triangles. Experiment with building shapes of specific area or perimeter, and explore how scaling a shape affects these properties. Whether you're solving puzzles or designing your own shapes, Area Builder offers a fun, interactive way to master the concepts of area and perimeter!

Should LBJ run for a second term? How might President Lincoln respond to the situation at Ft. Sumter? What can President Jefferson do about the Port of New Orleans?

Your students will take on the job of advising the president through historical events and challenges by talking to people in and around the White House. Consult with confidants within the White House and use evidence-based reasoning to provide a presidential briefing.

Can your students advise Presidents Jefferson, Lincoln, and Johnson on landmark events and important historical decisions that defined their presidencies? 

In Brief the Chief, your students will:

  • Select from three presidencies: Thomas Jefferson, Abraham Lincoln, and Lyndon B. Johnson

  • Choose from 6 historical challenges

  • Interview stakeholders and collect notes

  • Make an informed position and present it for consideration

  • Discover the historical outcomes of each challenge

Made in partnership with The White House Historical Association.

Race to Ratify drops your students into 1787, where the ink is still drying on the new Constitution. Will it become the law of the land or will it fall into the dustbin of history? The fate of the young nation is in their hands! Use this game to teach the big ideas at the core of the ratification debate between the Federalists and Anti-Federalists.

Dive deep into the heated national debate over the future of a radical new plan for the American government and explore big ideas at the core of the ratification debate between the Federalists and Anti-Federalists.

Students will travel across the 13 states to hear from a diverse and opinionated cast of characters and use what they learn to influence others through the social media of the time...pamphlets. Can your students be ratification influencers?

Social Media is everywhere. It can be a great source of news and information, but not all content is created equal. Are your students prepared to separate good information from bad? NewsFeed Defenders sharpens students' news literacy skills.

Welcome to Newsably, a fictional social media site focused on news and information. As NewsFeed Defenders, your students are on a mission to maintain the site and grow traffic. In order to be successful, students will learn the elements of high-quality journalism and markers of deceptive posts. Your students will need to spot fake posts that try to sneak in through hidden ads, viral deception, and false reporting.

live_items.body:
Welcome to the neighborhood! We’ve got a lot of great people and more than a few challenges. Can your students devise solutions that reflect the community's needs and resources?

Challenge your students to solve familiar problems and discover how they can impact their community by playing Neighborhood Good. Students will select issues within a fictional community that resonates with them, speak with neighbors to better understand the issue, and develop a plan of action. Students can address three different challenges or revisit a challenge to try different solutions.

Show your students how civic engagement works as they discover the level of impact they can make.

neighborhood-good.card_excerpt: Meet with your neighbors, make a plan, and do some Neighborhood Good.

live_items.body:
Welcome to Congress, are your students ready to explore the legislative process as they craft a bill?

Students will select a district to represent in the House of Representatives and get to know their constituents by reviewing letters and digging into survey data.

When they select an issue that's important to the people who live in their district, it is time for them to jump into the law-making process! Students will take their issue to the House and start crafting their bill.

Can they make the compromises necessary to get the bill passed by the House and Senate and make a law, all while balancing their constituents' needs?

In Immigration Nation, your students will identify which would-be U.S. residents are citizens or eligible for immigration. Connect newcomers to the immigration rule that applies to their situation and guide newcomers along their path to naturalization and citizenship.

In Executive Command, they can be president for four years! Being commander in chief and chief executive is no easy job! Students must strategically balance running a government and accomplishing their agenda with the challenges and responsibilities that crop up along the way. They will propose an agenda to Congress, sign bills into law, delegate new laws to the appropriate federal agency, handle international diplomacy, and command the military during times of war.

Are they up for the challenge?

live_items.body:
Invite your students to step into their new law firm, which specializes in constitutional law.

In Do I Have a Right?, students decide if potential clients have had their constitutional rights violated, match them with the best lawyer, and try to win their case in court. The more clients students serve, the faster their law firm grows!

Students can play two ways:

  • The full edition covers rights found across all constitutional amendments.

  • The Bill of Rights edition focuses on the rights addressed in the first ten amendments.

Get ready to answer the question: Do I have a right?

Allow your students to explore our state and federal court systems by helping their passengers navigate the U.S. judicial system.

In Court Quest, students will pick up passengers, hear about how they need help from the judicial system, and identify the correct court for their case. Explore what the different courts do at the state and federal levels and discover the complexities within the judicial system.

Can your students help passengers navigate the U.S. judicial system?

Let your students try their hand at running their own county government in Texas. Students will create and run their very own county and work across departments to turn their ideas into reality.

In Counties Work: Texas, students will discover what the Texas county government does while stepping into the role of a county official. Students will stay on top of resident requests, manage the annual budget through tax adjustments and spending choices, and address community crises that pop up along the way. Students will see what county departments have solutions as they work to balance the budget and keep citizens happy.

Each branch plays a specific role in turning an idea into a law. In Branches of Power, your students will practice their decision-making skills as they take on the roles and responsibilities of the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial Branches and turn as many bills into laws as possible. Through the game, players will introduce a presidential agenda, communicate with the public, write legislation, sign or veto bills, and even judge passed laws.

In Branches of Power your students will:

  • Create a presidential agenda and learn about the executive branch powers

  • Introduce bills and pass laws out of Congress

  • Apply judicial review to passed laws

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In Argument Wars, your students will practice their argumentation and persuasion skills with a real case that made it all the way to the U.S. Supreme Court. They’ll pick a side to represent, identify the Constitutional basis for the case, and dive in. The other lawyer is the competition, and whoever has the strongest arguments wins!

Argue one of these Supreme Court Cases:

  • Bond v. United States

  • Brown v. Board of Education

  • Gideon v. Wainwright

  • Hazelwood v. Kuhlmeier

  • In Re Gault

  • Miranda v. Arizona

  • New Jersey v. T.L.O.

  • Snyder v. Phelps 

  • Texas v. Johnson

While the game is based on real cases and historical arguments, it is not a reenactment. The outcome of the game is up to your student’s arguments. In the end, they will discover how the real justices voted.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
Constitutional Compromise challenges your students to find a way forward for a young nation as disagreements mount. They will engage in the ideas discussed at the Constitutional Convention of 1787 and discover the compromises made by the 55 delegates.

Your students will hear from delegates as they cast their vision for the future of the United States, balance the interests of a diverse set of states, and navigate the interests of delegates who envision vastly different roles for the new government. In Constitutional Compromise, your students will:

  • Experience the main historical debates of the Constitutional Convention

  • Identify points from each side of a debate to build a compromise

  • Discover the modern relevance of each compromise and how they compare to historical outcomes

Not all compromises are (or were) the ideal outcomes. While based on real debates and historical arguments, Constitutional Compromise is not a historical reenactment. In the end, your students will discover what really happened in Philadelphia in 1787.

They will engage with members of the National Security Council to weigh the pros and cons of various policy options and make foreign policy decisions. They will address international crises through strategic action and work to improve core metrics of U.S. prosperity, values, security, and world health.

Can your students make the tough choices as conflicts around the world escalate?

Blockly Games is a series of educational games that teach programming. It is designed for children who have not had prior experience with computer programming. By the end of these games, one is ready to use conventional text-based languages.

Blockly Games encourages the development of tomorrow's programmers. Designed to be self-paced, Blockly Games can be downloaded for offline use, ensuring accessibility for all students and technology. live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
In this strategic building game, you’ve decided to build a new town called Lakeland. In order to grow your town and keep your people alive, you need food and resources.

Luckily, you’ve got some friendly advisors to help you get started. Your Farm Advisor shows you how to grow corn. Now your people have food! Then you start a dairy farm. People love dairy. Milk, cheese, ice cream… what could go wrong?

As it turns out, a lot. Cows don’t just produce milk. They also produce lots and lots of poop, which means the lakes your people love are about to turn into a toxic cesspool of blue-green algae. Your mission: grow your town without destroying their lakes.

This game puts kids in charge of building their own town. Players add houses and farms, export produce, and manage resources like food, money, and manure. Students will get an introduction to the complex relationship between farming, soil nutrition, and lake pollution.

Want to learn more about Lakeland and Victor Zavala's research? Read the Story

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
Play as Jo Wilder, a scrappy girl who spends her days with her pet badger Teddy and her grandpa, a historian. When some mysterious artifacts show up at the History Museum, you must unravel the clues to find the real stories behind the artifacts.

Students will engage with the game as a tool for critical thinking and historical inquiry. As the plot unfolds, players come across primary source materials. They use the same skills as real historians: investigation, identification, corroboration and contextualizing evidence. To win each challenge, players must piece together the evidence to argue their case.

Jo Wilder and the Capitol Case, a historical inquiry adventure game, was designed with a cohort of third, fourth and fifth grade social studies teachers and tested by students throughout the state of Wisconsin.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body:
You are a material scientist who just crash-landed on an abandoned mining planet. You’re out of fuel, and your suit’s oxygen is running low. You need to mine enough fuel to power your ship, or you won’t survive.

You stumble into the old mining facility. That’s where you meet MAL, the mine’s Artificial Intelligence, who is thrilled to have someone to talk to. With MAL’s help, you’ll build scientific models to predict if you’re mining fast enough and what you need to do next.

Each level puts the student in the role of the scientific modeler. Students will set up equations, work with graphs, input data, and use models to make predictions. Along the way, as obstacles keep popping up, students will experience how models are used as a tool to make decisions.

live_items.title: About this game
live_items.body: In Bloom: The Saga of the Poop Fertilizer Economy, players serve as the director of SAGA:The Sustainable Agricultural Growth Administration. In this role, their goal is to foster economic growth across five different counties while reducing agricultural runoff and gross algal blooms. To win, players must develop local trade networks, employ a range of economic and environmental policies, and balance the needs and perspectives of bickering townsfolk. A key focus of the game is learning about the relationship between agricultural runoff and water quality, while exploring how markets that allow farmers to sell excess manure can lead to cleaner water and economic sustainability.
